book.title: Planet Palm: How Palm Oil Ended Up in Everything and Endangered the World
book.summary: Finalist, Helen Bernstein Book Award for Excellence in Journalism In the tradition of Eric Schlosser's Fast Food Nation, a groundbreaking global investigation into the industry ravaging the environment and global health—from the James Beard Award–winning journalist Over the past few decades, palm oil has seeped into every corner of our lives. Worldwide, palm oil production has nearly doubled in just the last decade: oil-palm plantations now cover an area nearly the size of New Zealand, and some form of the commodity lurks in half the products on U.S. grocery shelves. But the palm oil revolution has been built on stolen land and slave labor; it’s swept away cultures and so devastated the landscapes of Southeast Asia that iconic animals now teeter on the brink of extinction. Fires lit to clear the way for plantations spew carbon emissions to rival those of industrialized nations.

argument.statement: Palm oil’s spread into everyday products has been built on stolen land and slave labor, and clearing for plantations has devastated Southeast Asia’s landscapes and harmed global health and wildlife.

book.rationale: The book primarily investigates the environmental impacts of the palm oil industry, making Nature & Environment the dominant subject, while also addressing political and societal issues related to its production.
